ownership_reason: Only the gold records column keys: hops 1, 2 and 4 pass their arguments along unchanged and hop 3 only chooses the row (the row with the key, or a new row appended to the table) and never touches the column keys. The gold's javadoc promises that the column key is made one of the columns of the table; on an update of an object in an existing column the variant appends that key a second time, so the table reports a phantom column (getColumnCount() is columnKeys.size()), and removeObject, which removes an emptied column key once, leaves it behind. No one-line edit above the gold restores the contract while keeping every method used as documented: a hop can keep the gold from appending only by not calling it (the object is then not stored, or the hop stores it itself), by handing it another list (the gold's column-key output becomes dead), or by removing the key before the call, which moves the column to the end of the table on every update, against the hops' javadoc ('An update leaves the existing rows and columns where they are'). The convention is pinned outside the gold: DefaultKeyedValues2D.setValue, the sibling table of Numbers, appends a column key only when columnKeys.indexOf(columnKey) < 0 (DefaultKeyedValues2DTests testRemoveValueBug1690654: the same add / add / remove sequence gives getColumnCount() 2 then 1; testColumnCount); KeyedObjects.setObject, the row the gold writes into, replaces the object under an existing key instead of adding a second entry (KeyedObjectsTests testSetObject); KeyedObjects2D.getColumnCount returns the size of the column-key list.
